Document Title: Qualification and validation test methodology of the open-source CubeSat FloripaSat-I
Authors: M. G. Mariano; F. E. Morsch; M. S. Vega; D. M. A. M. Pio; S. L. Oriel; S. L. Kessler; B. E. Augusto
Author Affiliations: Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil; Department of Electrical Engineering, Federal University of Santa Catarina, Florianopolis, Brazil
Publication Title: Journal of Systems Engineering and Electronics
Abstract: The FloripaSat-I project consists of an initiative from the Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC), in Brazil, to train students to design, test and integrate innovative space systems. The group just developed its first open-source CubeSat, the FloripaSat-I, which aims to empower students to develop space systems through a practical approach, where they have full control of the design and test of a real spacecraft. The project has already gone through all the stages of a CubeSat mission prior to the launching and operation stages. A prototype of the satellite, as well the engineering models 1 and 2 (EM-I and EM-II) were built. The expertise provided by the engineering models allows the development of a functional flight model (FM). This paper presents the validation and qualification tests that pass various FloripaSat-I models, from the engineering model to the flight model. All stages of the project are described, the tests performed in each phase, as well as the lessons learned. Thus, this paper serves as a guidance for other university teams that want to test their own CubeSats, as well as teams that want to use the open-source hardware and software left as heritage by this project.

Document Title: A Framework for Resilient Power Systems in Cansat-class Reusable Small Satellites
Authors: B. Ahammed; M. A. I. Aion; M. Rafi; S. Ahmed; M. T. Reza; M. S. Rahman; M. A. Hossain
Author Affiliations: Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh; Department of Avionics Engineering, Aviation and Aerospace University Bangladesh, Lalmonirhat, Bangladesh
Publication Title: 2025 26th International Middle East Power Systems Conference (MEPCON)
Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an Electrical Power System for recoverable small-satellite platforms used in educational and experimental missions. General orbital CubeSats, which are not designed to be retrieved after launch, differ from CanSat-class payloads and balloon-based test vehicles, which can be recovered. The proposed framework ReSS-EPS (Electrical Power System for Reusable Small Satellites) integrates mission load profiling, analytical power budgeting, converter-aware simulations using MATLAB and modular PCB design to connect conceptual design with practical hardware. MATLAB simulation results characterize converter efficiency, battery charge-discharge dynamics and characteristics, and runtime margins and provide guidance for architecture optimization. The hardware design utilizes dual Li-ion storage to maintain a reliable power supply, preventing power loss during periods of high current consumption. It features regulated power rails and includes an isolated recovery module to provide redundancy. The implemented system achieves reliable operation with validated runtime margins and fault-tolerant recovery, demonstrating ReSS-EPS as a cost-effective and reusable solution for small satellite missions.

Document Title: Applying Model-Based Systems Engineering on CubeSat Budget Calculating
Author Affiliations: School of Computer Science, Netanya Academic College, Netanya, Israel
Abstract: This work presents a tool based on Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) for automating the process of budget calculation - mass, volume, power, and energy - for CubeSat nanosatellites based on user input which can be iteratively fine-tuned to fit the CubeSat limitations. CubeSat is a standard that defines nanosatellites with a base unit (1U) measuring ${10 \times 10 \times 10}$ and a maximum weight of up to 2 kg per 1U. They are cost-effective due to their use of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components. This modularity provides flexibility on component selection to conform to the standard constraints that are forced by budget calculation. Modularity is fundamental in systems engineering design, which adopts a holistic approach to create systems by integrating various components and considering their interactions. CubeSat follows this approach. Object Process Methodology (OPM) and Systems Modeling Language (SysML) are popular modeling languages for systems engineering. This work benefits from MBSE for nanosatellite budget calculation. Specifically, it uses OPM to conceptually model it, applies OPM's computational capabilities on the produced model to calculate its budgets using OPM's coding capabilities, and eventually visually simulates the model by OPM's execution feature.
